chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, may Allah be pleased with him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Isma’il, from al-Khurasani, meaning al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Abstinence (al-himyah) from something is not by abandoning it completely; rather, abstinence from something is to take little from it.

key_terms.الْإِقْلَالُ: Taking little, reducing, or consuming in small amounts
key_terms.الْخُرَاسَانِي: A title for Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to his residence in Khurasan
key_terms.حِمْيَة: Abstinence, restraint, or moderation in consumption

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between total abstinence and moderation in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that true abstinence (himyah) is not total avoidance but rather moderation and consuming in small amounts, a nuance highlighted in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*. This teaching aligns with the Shia emphasis on *wasatiyyah* (centrism), rejecting both excess and extreme asceticism in favor of balanced engagement with worldly matters.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, may Allah be pleased with him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammed, from Ibrahim bin Ishaq, from Abdullah bin Ahmad, from Isma’eel, from al-Khurasani, meaning al-Rida, peace be upon him, that he said:
Abstinence from something is not by abandoning it. Abstinence form something is only to take little from it.
